topics.title: Maxwell's Equations and Boundary Conditions
topics.syllabus: Maxwell's Equations: Differential and integral forms and their interpretation, boundary conditions, wave equation, Poynting vector.

cards.title: The four equations, both forms
cards.bodyHtml: The displacement-current term ∂D/∂t\partial D/\partial t∂D/∂t is Maxwell's own addition and the reason waves exist at all. In statics it vanishes and the electric and magnetic sets decouple — which is exactly what a question means when it says 'static fields'.
cards.pitfallHtml: A field given as a candidate BBB must satisfy ∇⋅B=0\nabla\cdot B=0∇⋅B=0; a candidate static EEE must satisfy ∇×E=0\nabla\times E=0∇×E=0. Questions that ask 'which of these can be a valid field' are answered by one divergence or one curl, nothing more.

formulas.exprHtml: ∇⋅D=ρv ⇔ ∮D⋅dS=Qenc\nabla\cdot D=\rho_v\ \Leftrightarrow\ \oint D\cdot dS=Q_{enc}∇⋅D=ρv​ ⇔ ∮D⋅dS=Qenc​
formulas.noteHtml: Gauss's law

formulas.exprHtml: ∇⋅B=0 ⇔ ∮B⋅dS=0\nabla\cdot B=0\ \Leftrightarrow\ \oint B\cdot dS=0∇⋅B=0 ⇔ ∮B⋅dS=0
formulas.noteHtml: no magnetic monopoles

formulas.exprHtml: ∇×E=−∂B∂t ⇔ ∮E⋅dl=−dΦdt\nabla\times E=-\dfrac{\partial B}{\partial t}\ \Leftrightarrow\ \oint E\cdot dl=-\dfrac{d\Phi}{dt}∇×E=−∂t∂B​ ⇔ ∮E⋅dl=−dtdΦ​
formulas.noteHtml: Faraday

formulas.exprHtml: ∇×H=J+∂D∂t ⇔ ∮H⋅dl=Ienc+Id\nabla\times H=J+\dfrac{\partial D}{\partial t}\ \Leftrightarrow\ \oint H\cdot dl=I_{enc}+I_d∇×H=J+∂t∂D​ ⇔ ∮H⋅dl=Ienc​+Id​

formulas.noteHtml: continuity — implied by the set, not independent

cards.title: Boundary conditions
cards.bodyHtml: Tangential EEE and normal BBB are always continuous. The other two jump by whatever free surface charge or current sits on the interface — at a perfect conductor, that jump is the whole answer.

cards.title: Wave equation and the Poynting vector
cards.bodyHtml: S=E×HS=E\times HS=E×H points where the power flows and its magnitude is the power density in W/m². For a uniform plane wave it lies along the direction of propagation, and its time average is what a power meter reads.

topics.title: Plane Waves, Media and Interfaces

cards.bodyHtml: Read polarisation off the two orthogonal components: equal amplitudes at ±90∘\pm90^\circ±90∘ give circular, anything else elliptical, zero phase difference linear. Phase velocity may exceed ccc; group velocity, which carries the information, never does.

topics.title: Transmission Lines and Matching
topics.syllabus: Transmission Lines: Equations, characteristic impedance, impedance matching, impedance transformation, S-parameters, Smith chart.

cards.pitfallHtml: A lossless three-port cannot be simultaneously matched at all ports and reciprocal — the standard proof-style question. The circulator escapes it by being non-reciprocal.

topics.title: Waveguides, Fibres and Antennas
topics.syllabus: Rectangular and circular waveguides, light propagation in optical fibers, dipole and monopole antennas, linear antenna arrays.

cards.title: Rectangular waveguide
cards.bodyHtml: A hollow guide is a high-pass filter: nothing below the cutoff of its lowest mode propagates. With a>ba>ba>b, the dominant mode is TE10\mathrm{TE}_{10}TE10​ and its cutoff depends only on the broad wall.
cards.pitfallHtml: Below cutoff the mode is evanescent, not absorbed: γ\gammaγ is purely real, the field decays exponentially and no power flows. That is different from attenuation by loss.
